name: Credential Hunting - Configs, Keys and Secrets
description: Hunt stored credentials across config files, app configs (e.g. WordPress wp-config.php), and SSH key directories. Recovered keys/passwords enable lateral movement or direct root.

defense.why_it_works: Credentials are frequently stored in plaintext in config files, shell history, and web application configs. Low-privileged users can read these files if permissions are too permissive. wp-config.php, .bash_history, SSH keys, and .conf files often contain database passwords, API keys, and SSH private keys readable by any local user.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access as a low-privileged user. World-readable or group-readable config files, history files, or SSH directories.
defense.impact: Credential discovery enables lateral movement (reuse across services), vertical escalation (database root access, sudo with found password), or pivoting to other hosts via SSH keys.
defense.detection: Auditd: file open syscalls on sensitive paths (/var/www/html/wp-config.php, ~/.bash_history, ~/.ssh/id_rsa) by unexpected users. SIEM: alert on reads of config files by non-owner non-service users.
defense.artifacts: Auditd log: open() on wp-config.php or .bash_history | File access audit trail | SSH audit log if key used
defense.prevention: Apply strict file permissions: wp-config.php chmod 640, owned by www-data. Never log credentials in bash history (set HISTFILE=/dev/null in sensitive scripts). Store secrets in a secrets manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager). Use SSH agent forwarding instead of copying private keys. Enable SELinux/AppArmor to restrict file access by process.
defense.misconfiguration: wp-config.php is world-readable. Bash history files are world-readable. SSH private keys stored with permissions wider than 600. Config files containing credentials left in publicly readable web directories.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# World-readable wp-config.php
-rw-r--r-- 1 www-data www-data 3014 /var/www/html/wp-config.php
# Contains: define('DB_PASSWORD', 'ClearTextPass!');

# World-readable bash_history
-rw-rw-r-- 1 admin admin ~/.bash_history
defense.secure_config:
# Restrict wp-config.php
chmod 640 /var/www/html/wp-config.php
chown www-data:www-data /var/www/html/wp-config.php

# Clear history and prevent logging
unset HISTFILE
export HISTFILE=/dev/null

# SSH key permissions
chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_rsa
chmod 700 ~/.ssh/
defense.evasion: Search config files without touching .bash_history first (avoid leaving traces). Use find with -readable flag to discover accessible files quietly.
